rows.jp: 去年の初夏だった。
rows.en: Early summer of last year.

ghs.en: It was last year, early Summer,

rows.jp: 新川豊と出会ったのは。
rows.en: That was when I met Yutaka Shinkawa.

ghs.en: when I had my meeting with Shinkawa Yutaka.

rows.jp: 蝉のうるさい夏だった。
rows.en: A summer loud with cicadas.

ghs.en: It was a Summer of loud cicadas.

rows.jp: 偶然、ぶつかった。
rows.en: We bumped into each other by chance.

ghs.en: We bumped into each other, a coincidence.

rows.jp: 妙に会話が弾んで。
rows.en: By chance, we crossed paths.

ghs.en: An odd conversation was stimulated.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that their conversation became strangely lively. The English makes the conversation itself odd and treats it as something externally stimulated.

rows.jp: ウマがあった。
rows.en: For some reason, conversation came easily.

ghs.en: We got along well, as if a rider and his horse.
ghs.assessment: ウマが合う is an idiom meaning that they hit it off. The English translates that meaning and then redundantly exposes the source idiom as a new literal comparison.

highlights.text: as if a rider and his horse

rows.jp: 群青には完全に自分の世界で生きている者もいる。
rows.en: Some people at Gunjo live entirely within worlds of their own.

ghs.en:
In Gunjou, there are people who live entirely
into their world,
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that some people at Gunjou live entirely in worlds of their own. GHS uses the wrong preposition in live entirely into their world. Gunjou itself is an acceptable ASCII long-vowel spelling and is not part of the error.
ghs.remedy: Use live entirely in worlds of their own.

rows.jp: 人を傷つけやすい者もいる。
rows.en: Some are prone to hurting others.

ghs.en: as well as people who easily hurt others.

rows.jp: ある頃から、世界は狂人を生み出しはじめた。
rows.en: At some point, the world began producing madmen.

ghs.en:
Ever since a time, the world had begun to give
birth to madmen.
ghs.assessment: ある頃から means 'from a certain point' or 'at some point.' The English phrase is not idiomatic and past perfect lacks a later past anchor.

highlights.text: Ever since a time, the world had begun

rows.jp: その多くが人を傷つけた。
rows.en: Many of them hurt people.

ghs.en: Many of them injured people.

rows.jp: 心の病は、ただ己だけの問題ではなくなっていた。
rows.en: Mental illness was no longer a problem confined to the sufferer.

ghs.en:
The illness of the heart was no longer merely
a personal problem.
ghs.assessment: 心の病 here means mental illness, not a cardiac disease or a metaphorical illness of the heart.

rows.jp: 原因はわからない。
rows.en: No one knew why.

ghs.en: Origin is unknown.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says the cause is unknown. The English chooses a different noun and omits the required article.

rows.jp: 政府はいくつかの対策を打ち出したが、その内容が広く報道されることはなかった。
rows.en: The government rolled out several countermeasures, but the public was never told what they were.

ghs.en:
The government had worked out a number of
countermeasures, but the specifics of those
were not widely reported on.

rows.jp: 水面下で動いている、と曜子ちゃんは言っていた。
rows.en: Youko said things were happening behind the scenes.

ghs.en:
Motion beneath the water surface, said
Youko-chan. All behind closed doors.
ghs.assessment: Youko says that measures are moving below the surface. The English produces a subjectless fragment from the literal water image and then adds the separate idiom 'behind closed doors.'

highlights.text:
Motion beneath the water surface, said
Youko-chan. All behind closed doors.

rows.jp: 詳細は不明。
rows.en: The details were unknown.

ghs.en: Details are unclear.

rows.jp: 少なくとも、世界が緩慢な狂気に浸されていることは……自分の胸に聞けばよく理解できた。
rows.en: All I had to do was look inside myself to know the world was slowly drowning in madness.

ghs.en:
At the very least, the world was sinking into
a slow insanity... and if I listened to my
heart I could very well understand.

rows.jp: だから群青学院は存在した。
rows.en: That is why Gunjo Academy exists.

ghs.en: That is why Gunjou Institute existed.

rows.jp: 隔離施設として。
rows.en: As an isolation facility.

ghs.en: As an isolation facility.

rows.jp: 留年は日常茶飯事。
rows.en: As an isolation facility.

ghs.en: Repeating class years is an ordinary event.

rows.jp: だが何年かけても症状が回復しない者は、さらなる施設へと送られる。
rows.en: Repeating a year is routine.

ghs.en:
Yet, the people whose conditions do not recover
after some years are sent to a further facility.

rows.jp: そういう人々は、ほとんど他者との接触を必要としない。
rows.en: People like that have almost no need for contact with others.

ghs.en:
People like those require almost no contact
with others.

rows.jp: 独力で生きる力には欠けているが、当人の心は、もう人のそれを離れてしまっているのだ。
rows.en: They lack the ability to live on their own, yet their minds have already passed beyond what we would call human.

ghs.en:
Their power to live by their strength is lacking,
but their hearts are already distanced from
those of others.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says they lack the ability to live independently and that their minds have departed from the human kind. 'Live by their strength' misstates independence, while 'distanced from those of others' weakens the categorical second clause.

highlights.text:
Their power to live by their strength is lacking,
but their hearts are already distanced from
those of others.

rows.jp: だから。
rows.en: And so.

ghs.en: Therefore,

rows.jp: 群青では友達を作るのは、少し難しい。
rows.en: Making friends at Gunjo is a little difficult.

ghs.en: making friends in Gunjou is somewhat difficult.

rows.jp: 対話が成立しにくいからだ。
rows.en: Real conversation is hard to come by.

ghs.en:
Because it is difficult for dialogue to come
into existence.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that successful dialogue or communication is difficult. The English literalizes 成立 as a conversation coming into existence.

highlights.text:
for dialogue to come
into existence

rows.jp: １クラスで、１０人くらいだろうか。
rows.en: Maybe ten people in each class.

ghs.en: In one class, there are about ten people, maybe,

rows.jp: まともに会話が成り立つのは。
rows.en: That is about how many can carry on a normal conversation.

ghs.en: that can construct a normal conversation at all.
ghs.assessment: 会話が成り立つ means being able to hold or sustain a coherent conversation, not constructing one as an object.

rows.jp: 『ＯＫ、なんとかやっていけそうな気がしてきた』
rows.en: ‘Okay. I'm starting to think I might manage somehow.’

ghs.en: Shinkawa: 『Okieh, I got the feeling I can work with this somehow.』
ghs.assessment: The source begins with the English loan 'OK.' The invented eye-dialect spelling adds a voice not encoded by that form.

ghs.en: Taichi: "......"

rows.jp: 誰が悪かったのかな。
rows.en: Whose fault was it?

ghs.en: Whose fault was it, I wonder?

rows.jp: 俺か。
rows.en: Mine?

ghs.en: Mine?

rows.jp: それともヤツか。
rows.en: Or his?

ghs.en: Or was it his?

rows.jp: 結論は出ない。
rows.en: No answer comes.

ghs.en: Final words don't come.
ghs.assessment: 結論は出ない means that no conclusion presents itself. 'Final words' instead suggests a dying statement or the end of a speech.

rows.jp: 涙も出ない。
rows.en: No tears come, either.

ghs.en: Tears don't come.

rows.jp: まだ、出ない。
rows.en: Not yet.

ghs.en: They... still don't come.
